To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temperature‐sensitive mutant of P. chrysogenum can be used to produce high levels of penicillin for long periods of time in a 320‐L air‐lift fermentor.

the immobilization of a temperature‐sensitive mutant of P. chrysogenum on Celite and its growth at 30 °C in a large air‐lift fermentor overcame the problem encountered with the parent organism of the rapid accumulation of free cells and resulted in the production of penicillin and a precursor for over 500 h.
a temperature‐sensitive mutant was used to uncouple growth from penicillin synthesis and that the immobilization of this mutant resulted in a stable process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an immobilization technique which is capable of producing a stable, continuous, high‐yielding penicillin fermentation.
the large‐scale immobilized growth of P. chrysogenum in an air‐lifting fermenter.
the immobilization of a temperature‐sensitive Penicillium strain in an air‐ lift fermenter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the temperature‐sensitive cycle mutation of the P. chrysogenum strain P2 has been shown to be a useful tool for the immobilized growth of this strain in an air‐ lift fermenter, and that this system can be operated continuously for 500 h.
immobilized P. chrysogenum can be operated for long periods of time in an air‐ lift fermenter and that the immobilization technique has a potential for industrial application.
the immobilization of P. chrysogenum in an air‐ lift fermenter is feasible, and that this technique has potential for the large‐scale production of penicillin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the air‐lift reactor is a very promising device for the large‐scale cultivation of immobilized mycelia.
immobilized P. chrysogenum is capable of producing penicillin and other metabolites continuously in the presence of a high level of dissolved oxygen.
the temperature‐sensitive mutant is a useful organism for immobilization and that the use of an air‐lift fermentor is a useful method for immobilized cell reactor operation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of an air‐lift fermentor for large‐scale immobilized growth of Penicillius chrysogenum is feasible, and that the use of a temperature‐sensitive division cycle mutant of P. chrysogenum can be a useful tool to study the effects of immobilization on the physiology of this organism.
it is feasible to use a temperature‐sensitive growth mutant of a filamentous microorganism to produce a secondary metabolite in a large‐scale immobilized reactor.
the air‐lift reactor is suitable for the immobilization of filamentous fungi, even those with a temperature‐sensitive growth cycle.
